advice: For the full-tile path, compute row and column base pointers once per output tile, then use a constant-trip reduction loop with pointer increments instead of recomputing k*n+i and k*n+j addresses each step. Keep the existing predicated tail path for incomplete tiles and general n. At n=512, a specialized path can use a fixed 512-step reduction loop only when n==512; it must still advance pointers within valid bounds and leave other dimensions on the general path. This directly targets repeated address arithmetic and loop branches while retaining FP32 SME outer products and the four ZA tile selectors.
risks: The compiler may already strength-reduce these expressions, so the change may have no effect. Pointer increments can introduce off-by-one or out-of-bounds access errors, especially when the final reduction step advances past the valid object; avoid forming invalid pointers and check odd dimensions, n smaller than a tile, tail rows and columns, n<=0, and numerical error against the fixed tolerance. Any performance conclusion requires fresh AC paired controls; the supplied battery scores are noisy historical context.
